title: Microsoft 365 admin center: agent-level controls for pay-as-you-go
summary: Hold: the spending-policy automation lists policies rather than setting the agent spending limits described by its row, and its UI path omits the resource-policy choice. The Azure budget automation is a description rather than a command, and the claim that billing setup is documented only in the Microsoft 365 admin center conflicts with Microsoft's documented Power Platform alternative.

claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Admin Center: Agent-Level Controls for Pay-as-you-go

claims.quote: This feature introduces admin controls for managing AI agents on a consumption basis within Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.quote: Administrators can specify which users can access particular agents through pay-as-you-go

claims.claim: The documented legacy Copilot Chat and SharePoint billing policies do not expose the roadmap's per-agent metered-eligibility selection.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe this roadmap feature by its name as of November 2026.

claims.quote: On the Billing policies tab, select Add a billing policy. ... On the Choose users page, select All users or a Specific group.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path to 'Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Billing policies > Add a billing policy > Choose users'. The existing note already gives the choices on that wizard page; no extra fields or confirmation steps are needed.

claims.claim: No API equivalent was documented for creating these legacy billing policies and choosing their users.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Chat" "billing policy" "API" "create"; "SharePoint agents" "billing policy" "Graph". Opened setup, commerce setup, Cost Management overview and spendingPolicy reference; its user spending policies are not documented as these legacy billing policies.

claims.claim: The Copilot Chat billing-policy user choice is All users or a single specific group.
claims.quote: On the Choose users page, select All users or a Specific group. If you select Specific group, search for and add a single group.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy is the complete route to resource-based per-agent spending controls.
claims.quote: Enter a name for the policy, then select Resources as its scope. ... Specific resources: Choose Specific resources when particular agents need their own policy or billing method.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].ui.path to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources > Specific resources'. Amend the existing note to say: 'Select the agents, then set the monthly spending limit and optional per-agent limit and choose the billing method; for environment scope, choose Specific environments or All environments instead.' This preserves the documented policy-type choice rather than ending before it.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies provides automation for setting individual Copilot Studio agent or environment spending limits and billing methods.
claims.quote: Get a list of spendingPolicy objects. ... Don't supply a request body for this method.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api to null and remove 'The API call lists policies and is not the full configuration equivalent' from its note. A read-only list is not the automation for this configuring row, even with that disclaimer. Searches for graph costManagement resource based spending policy perAgentLimit Copilot Studio API and reads of the resource, list, update and overview references found user-audience policies, not a documented write equivalent for this resource-based control. Do not substitute their identity-policy PATCH operation for agent limits.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies can set spending limits and billing methods for individual Copilot Studio agents or environments.
claims.quote: Manage Copilot Studio spending in the Microsoft 365 admin center by creating policies for environments or individual agents. You can set spending limits, choose a billing method, and monitor Copilot Credit usage.

claims.claim: For covered Copilot Studio agents or environments, Microsoft 365 spending policies take precedence over Power Platform admin center controls.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat SharePoint agents spending policies declarative. claims.claim: Resource-based policies do not apply to AI Builder features or the credits those features consume.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management budget creation is under Monitoring > Budgets.

claims.fix: Set controls[6].ui.path to 'scope > Monitoring > Budgets' and add to its existing note: 'Select the subscription used for SharePoint agents as the Cost Management scope.' The omitted subscription selection is an item-selection step, not a different control.

claims.claim: Create a budget in Microsoft Cost Management with a Bicep file or ARM template is an executable automation call.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure subscription deploy budget Bicep az deployment sub create main.bicep startDate endDate contactEmails. Opened SharePoint billing and Create a budget with Bicep; the printed text describes a technique, not an operation or command.
claims.fix: Replace controls[6].api with kind 'azure-cli', call 'az deployment sub create --name <deployment-name> --location <location> --template-file main.bicep --parameters startDate=<start-date> endDate=<end-date> contactEmails=<contact-emails-array>', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/quick-create-budget-bicep'. Add to the existing note: 'Save the quickstart No filter Bicep template as main.bicep and deploy against the billing subscription, supplying its start date, end date and contact email array.'
